title: 2002 HMMT February Algebra Problem 6
statement: Find the sum of the even positive divisors of 1000 .

solutions.text: 2184 . Notice that \(2 k\) is a divisor of 1000 iff \(k\) is a divisor of 500 , so we need only find the sum of the divisors of 500 and multiply by 2 . This can be done by enumerating the divisors individually, or simply by using the formula: \(\sigma\left(2^{2} \cdot 5^{3}\right)=\left(1+2+2^{2}\right)(1+5+\) \(\left.5^{2}+5^{3}\right)=1092\), and then doubling gives 2184. Alternate Solution: The sum of all the divisors of 1000 is \(\left(1+2+2^{2}+2^{3}\right)\left(1+5+5^{2}+5^{3}\right)=2340\). The odd divisors of 1000 are simply the divisors of 125 , whose sum is \(1+5+5^{2}+5^{3}=156\); subtracting this from 2340 , we are left with the sum of the even divisors of 1000 , which is 2184 .
